title: Publication-quality activation tables
text: cluster_table() fmrireport’s standalone function building publication-quality activation tables statistical brain volume. follows COBIDAS reporting guidelines: hierarchical cluster/sub-peak structure, world coordinates, p-values, optional anatomical labeling. vignette walks creating realistic synthetic activations, detecting clusters, formatting tables, adding atlas labels.

title: Publication-quality activation tables
text: Real fMRI analyses produce NeuroVol objects fmrireg similar packages. demonstration, ’ll build synthetic t-statistic volume Gaussian-shaped activation blobs placed known locations. Now add Gaussian-shaped activation blobs. ’ll place grid coordinates use smooth falloff simulate realistic spatial extent: Let’s visualize synthetic activation map:
code: library(fmrireport) library(neuroim2) #> Loading required package: Matrix #>  #> Attaching package: 'neuroim2' #> The following object is masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     scale  # Define a brain-like volume in MNI-ish space # 2mm isotropic, 91x109x91 grid, origin at (-90, -126, -72) sp <- NeuroSpace(c(91, 109, 91),                  spacing = c(2, 2, 2),                  origin = c(-90, -126, -72))  # Start with Gaussian noise (simulating a t-stat map under the null) set.seed(2024) arr <- array(rnorm(prod(dim(sp))), dim(sp)) # Helper: add a 3D Gaussian blob centered at grid coordinate (cx, cy, cz) add_gaussian_blob <- function(arr, cx, cy, cz, peak_value, sigma = 4) {   dims <- dim(arr)   # Work in a local window for efficiency   radius <- ceiling(3 * sigma)   x_range <- max(1, cx - radius):min(dims[1], cx + radius)   y_range <- max(1, cy - radius):min(dims[2], cy + radius)   z_range <- max(1, cz - radius):min(dims[3], cz + radius)    for (xi in x_range) {     for (yi in y_range) {       for (zi in z_range) {         d2 <- (xi - cx)^2 + (yi - cy)^2 + (zi - cz)^2         arr[xi, yi, zi] <- arr[xi, yi, zi] +           peak_value * exp(-d2 / (2 * sigma^2))       }     }   }   arr }  # Place blobs at grid coordinates that map to known cortical MNI regions. # With origin=(-90,-126,-72) and spacing=2mm: #   grid (27,51,65) -> MNI (-38,-26,56) = Left SomMot #   grid (65,51,65) -> MNI ( 38,-26,56) = Right SomMot #   grid (46,55,67) -> MNI (  0,-18,62) = Medial motor #   grid (41,21,39) -> MNI (-10,-86, 4) = Left V1 #   grid (51,21,39) -> MNI ( 10,-86, 4) = Right V1  # Blob 1: Left somatomotor cortex (large, strong activation) arr <- add_gaussian_blob(arr, cx = 27, cy = 51, cz = 65, peak_value = 8, sigma = 5)  # Blob 2: Right somatomotor cortex (moderate) arr <- add_gaussian_blob(arr, cx = 65, cy = 51, cz = 65, peak_value = 6, sigma = 4)  # Blob 3: Medial motor / SMA (moderate) arr <- add_gaussian_blob(arr, cx = 46, cy = 55, cz = 67, peak_value = 5.5, sigma = 3)  # Blob 4: Left primary visual cortex (small, strong) arr <- add_gaussian_blob(arr, cx = 41, cy = 21, cz = 39, peak_value = 7, sigma = 3)  # Blob 5: Right primary visual cortex (small, moderate) arr <- add_gaussian_blob(arr, cx = 51, cy = 21, cz = 39, peak_value = 5, sigma = 3)  vol <- NeuroVol(arr, sp) # Show axial slices at the levels where we placed blobs slices <- c(39, 55, 60, 65, 67) plot_montage(vol, zlevels = slices, along = 3L,              cmap = "inferno", ncol = 5L,              title = "Synthetic t-statistic map")

title: Publication-quality activation tables
text: Detect clusters t > 3.0 default settings: output shows: Cluster ID size (voxels mm^3) Peak coordinates world space (mm) Peak statistic p-value Sub-peaks (local maxima) indented cluster

title: Publication-quality activation tables
text: local_maxima_dist parameter sets minimum distance (mm) reported sub-peaks. larger value gives fewer, distinct peaks:
code: # Tight distance: many sub-peaks ct_tight <- cluster_table(vol, threshold = 3.0, stat_type = "t", df = 100,                           local_maxima_dist = 8, max_peaks = 5) cat("Sub-peaks with 8mm distance:\n") #> Sub-peaks with 8mm distance: nrow(ct_tight$peaks) #> [1] 20  # Wide distance: fewer sub-peaks ct_wide <- cluster_table(vol, threshold = 3.0, stat_type = "t", df = 100,                          local_maxima_dist = 25, max_peaks = 5) cat("Sub-peaks with 25mm distance:\n") #> Sub-peaks with 25mm distance: nrow(ct_wide$peaks) #> [1] 20

title: Publication-quality activation tables
text: default, clusters sorted size (descending). can sort peak statistic instead:
code: ct_by_stat <- cluster_table(vol, threshold = 3.0, stat_type = "t", df = 100,                             sort_by = "peak_stat") # First cluster has the highest absolute peak stat ct_by_stat$clusters[, c("cluster_id", "k", "peak_stat")] #>   cluster_id    k peak_stat #> 1          1 1623  9.166727 #> 2          3  483  8.573392 #> 3          2  530  8.085848 #> 4          4  187  6.480548

title: Publication-quality activation tables
text: cluster_table() computes voxel-level p-values peak statistic degrees freedom. Different statistic types supported:
code: # t-statistic ct_t <- cluster_table(vol, threshold = 3.0, stat_type = "t", df = 100) head(ct_t$clusters[, c("peak_stat", "peak_p")]) #>   peak_stat       peak_p #> 1  9.166727 6.635204e-15 #> 2  8.085848 1.485288e-12 #> 3  8.573392 1.307328e-13 #> 4  6.480548 3.481219e-09  # z-statistic (provide df to enable p-value computation) ct_z <- cluster_table(vol, threshold = 3.0, stat_type = "z", df = 1) head(ct_z$clusters[, c("peak_stat", "peak_p")]) #>   peak_stat       peak_p #> 1  9.166727 4.876005e-20 #> 2  8.085848 6.173336e-16 #> 3  8.573392 1.004808e-17 #> 4  6.480548 9.138986e-11  # Without df, p-values are NA ct_nodf <- cluster_table(vol, threshold = 3.0, stat_type = "t", df = NULL) head(ct_nodf$clusters[, c("peak_stat", "peak_p")]) #>   peak_stat peak_p #> 1  9.166727     NA #> 2  8.085848     NA #> 3  8.573392     NA #> 4  6.480548     NA

title: Publication-quality activation tables
text: can pair cluster table brain overlay visualization:
code: # Create a thresholded overlay for visualization arr_thresh <- as.array(vol) arr_thresh[abs(arr_thresh) < 3.0] <- NA vol_thresh <- NeuroVol(arr_thresh, sp)  # Create a background volume (uniform gray for this demo) bg_arr <- array(1000, dim(sp)) bg <- NeuroVol(bg_arr, sp)  plot_overlay(bg, vol_thresh,              zlevels = c(39, 55, 60, 65),              along = 3L,              ov_cmap = "inferno",              ov_thresh = 0,              ncol = 4L,              title = "Thresholded activation (t > 3.0)")

title: Publication-quality activation tables
text: default, clusters use 26-connectivity (face, edge, vertex neighbors). can switch conservative connectivity: Stricter connectivity (6-connect) tends break large clusters smaller pieces.
code: ct_6 <- cluster_table(vol, threshold = 3.0, stat_type = "t", df = 100,                       connectivity = "6-connect") ct_26 <- cluster_table(vol, threshold = 3.0, stat_type = "t", df = 100,                        connectivity = "26-connect") cat("6-connect clusters:", ct_6$n_clusters, "\n") #> 6-connect clusters: 4 cat("26-connect clusters:", ct_26$n_clusters, "\n") #> 26-connect clusters: 4

title: Publication-quality activation tables
text: function handles edge cases gracefully:
code: # No suprathreshold voxels ct_empty <- cluster_table(vol, threshold = 100) ct_empty$n_clusters #> [1] 0 print(ct_empty) #> cluster_table: 0 clusters (threshold = 100 )  # Very liberal threshold (many small clusters filtered by min_cluster_size) ct_liberal <- cluster_table(vol, threshold = 1.5, min_cluster_size = 50) cat("Clusters with k >= 50:", ct_liberal$n_clusters, "\n") #> Clusters with k >= 50: 20

title: Publication-quality activation tables
text: cluster_table() provides complete pipeline statistical volume publication-ready activation table: 1. Cluster detection via neuroim2::conn_comp() 2. Size filtering 3. World coordinate transformation 4. Sub-peak (local maxima) identification 5. Optional atlas labeling via neuroatlas 6. Parametric p-value computation Output can printed console, converted flat data.frame, formatted tinytable direct inclusion reports.

title: Getting started with fmrireport
text: fitting fMRI GLM fmrireg, typically need inspect model specification, visualize contrast maps, report peak activation coordinates. manually — extracting coefficient summaries, building brain montages, assembling cluster tables — tedious error-prone. fmrireport generates publication-ready PDF reports fitted fmri_lm object single function call. also provides standalone cluster_table() function building COBIDAS-compliant activation tables statistical brain volume.

title: Getting started with fmrireport
text: package two main entry points: report() — renders full PDF report (model info, design matrix, HRF shapes, parameter estimates, contrast maps peak tables, diagnostics). cluster_table() — standalone function detects suprathreshold clusters, identifies sub-peaks, computes p-values, optionally labels regions brain atlas.

title: Getting started with fmrireport
text: don’t need full fmri_lm fit use cluster_table(). NeuroVol containing statistical map . Now detect clusters print result: output shows cluster size, world coordinates, peak statistic, p-value. Sub-peaks (local maxima within cluster) indented beneath parent.
code: library(fmrireport) library(neuroim2) #> Loading required package: Matrix #>  #> Attaching package: 'neuroim2' #> The following object is masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     scale  # Create a synthetic t-stat volume with two activation clusters set.seed(42) sp <- NeuroSpace(c(64, 64, 40), spacing = c(3, 3, 3)) arr <- array(rnorm(64 * 64 * 40), c(64, 64, 40))  # Cluster 1: large blob in left hemisphere arr[20:28, 25:33, 15:22] <- arr[20:28, 25:33, 15:22] + 5  # Cluster 2: smaller blob in right hemisphere arr[40:46, 30:36, 20:26] <- arr[40:46, 30:36, 20:26] + 4  vol <- NeuroVol(arr, sp) ct <- cluster_table(vol, threshold = 3.0, stat_type = "t", df = 50) print(ct) #> cluster_table: 2 cluster(s)  |  threshold = 3.00 (t)  |  space = Unknown #>  #>   Cluster 1  (k = 638, 17226 mm3) #>     Peak:   x = 60.0  y = 81.0  z = 51.0  stat = 8.208  p = 7.936e-11 #>       sub-peak 2:  x = 60.0  y = 72.0  z = 45.0  stat = 7.870  p = 2.647e-10 #>       sub-peak 3:  x = 66.0  y = 87.0  z = 63.0  stat = 7.834  p = 3.008e-10 #>  #>   Cluster 2  (k = 281, 7587 mm3) #>     Peak:   x = 132.0  y = 96.0  z = 75.0  stat = 6.562  p = 2.905e-08 #>       sub-peak 2:  x = 132.0  y = 87.0  z = 57.0  stat = 6.416  p = 4.923e-08 #>       sub-peak 3:  x = 135.0  y = 105.0  z = 63.0  stat = 6.139  p = 1.329e-07

code: library(fmrireg)  # Fit a model (shown for context; not run here) fit <- fmri_lm(   onset ~ hrf(condition, contrasts = my_contrasts),   block = ~run,   dataset = my_dataset )  # Generate the report report(fit,        output_file = "my_analysis.pdf",        title = "Visual Localizer Analysis",        author = "Jane Doe",        cluster_thresh = 3.5,        min_cluster_size = 20L,        atlas = my_atlas)

title: Getting started with fmrireport
text: Two new parameters report() control cluster table: local_maxima_dist — minimum distance (mm) sub-peaks within cluster (default: 15) max_sub_peaks — maximum sub-peaks reported per cluster (default: 3)
code: report(fit,        output_file = "report.pdf",        local_maxima_dist = 12,        max_sub_peaks = 5)

title: Build a Publication-Quality Activation Cluster Table — cluster_table
text: vol NeuroVol object containing statistical map. threshold Numeric threshold cluster detection (absolute value). atlas Optional atlas object (e.g., volatlas neuroatlas) anatomical labeling. stat_type Type statistic volume: "t", "z", "F", "". df Degrees freedom p-value computation. single value t/z statistics, length-2 vector c(df1, df2) F statistics. NULL omits p-values. coord_space Character string naming coordinate space (e.g., "MNI152", "MNI305"). NULL, inferred atlas set "Unknown". min_cluster_size Minimum number voxels cluster retained. local_maxima_dist Minimum distance (mm) local maxima within cluster. max_peaks Maximum number sub-peaks reported per cluster. connectivity Voxel connectivity cluster detection. sort_by Sort clusters "size" (descending) "peak_stat" (descending absolute value).

title: Build a Publication-Quality Activation Cluster Table — cluster_table
text: S3 object class "cluster_table" elements: clusters data.frame one row per cluster. peaks data.frame sub-peaks (local maxima) per cluster. threshold threshold used. stat_type statistic type. df Degrees freedom. n_clusters Number clusters. coord_space Coordinate space label. atlas_name Name atlas used, NA.
